Let \(\angle ABC=2\theta\), so \(\angle KBC=\theta\). Let \(BC=x\) and \(CK=z\).

Since \(K\in AC\), triangle \(BCK\) is right at \(C\), so
\[
\tan\theta=\frac{CK}{BC}=\frac{z}{x}.
\]
Since \(BL=8\), \(CL=x-8\). In right triangle \(CKL\), \(\angle CKL=\theta\), so
\[
\tan\theta=\frac{CL}{CK}=\frac{x-8}{z}.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{z}{x}=\frac{x-8}{z}\implies z^2=x(x-8).
\]

By the angle bisector theorem,
\[
\frac{AK}{KC}=\frac{AB}{BC}=\frac{18}{x}.
\]
Let \(AC=y\). Then
\[
KC=z=\frac{xy}{x+18}.
\]
Also \(y^2=18^2-x^2=324-x^2\). Therefore
\[
z^2=\frac{x^2y^2}{(x+18)^2}=x(x-8).
\]
Substitute \(y^2=324-x^2\):
\[
x^2(324-x^2)=x(x-8)(x+18)^2.
\]
Divide by \(x\):
\[
x(324-x^2)=(x-8)(x+18)^2.
\]
Expanding gives
\[
x^3+14x^2-144x-1296=0
\]
\[
(x+18)(x^2-4x-72)=0.
\]
The valid positive root is
\[
x=2+2\sqrt{19}.
\]
Now in right triangle \(BCK\),
\[
KB^2=BC^2+CK^2=x^2+z^2=x^2+x(x-8)=2x(x-4).
\]
With \(x=2+2\sqrt{19}\),
\[
x(x-4)=2(1+\sqrt{19})\cdot 2(\sqrt{19}-1)=4(19-1)=72.
\]
Thus
\[
KB^2=2\cdot 72=144,
\]
so
\[
\boxed{KB=12}.
\]
